title: Getting started with clinstats
text: roc_summary() reports area curve together optimal operating point, odds_ratio() reports odds ratio high group Youden-optimal threshold. survival endpoint, survival_cutoff() estimates Kaplan-Meier Youden index grid candidate cut points returns best one.
code: marker <- scale(clin_crc$age) roc_summary(marker, clin_crc$rfs.event) #> # A tibble: 1 × 12 #>       n n_event   auc auc_ci_lower auc_ci_upper direction threshold sensitivity #>   <int>   <int> <dbl>        <dbl>        <dbl> <chr>         <dbl>       <dbl> #> 1  1698     574 0.514        0.485        0.542 >             0.143       0.493 #> # ℹ 4 more variables: specificity <dbl>, ppv <dbl>, npv <dbl>, accuracy <dbl> odds_ratio(marker, clin_crc$rfs.event) #> # A tibble: 1 × 9 #>   cutoff     n n_event n_high n_low odds_ratio ci_lower ci_upper p_value #>    <dbl> <int>   <int>  <int> <int>      <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1  0.143  1698     574    913   785      0.830    0.678     1.02  0.0697 survival_cutoff(   time = clin_crc$rfs.delay,   event = clin_crc$rfs.event,   marker = marker,   predict_time = 3 ) #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #>   cutoff  youden     tp     fp predict_time     n n_event #>    <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>        <dbl> <int>   <int> #> 1   1.49 -0.0181 0.0284 0.0465            3  1640     561

title: Curated colorectal cancer clinical data — clin_crc

what: Regression tables for clinical variables — cox_table
title: Regression tables for clinical variables — cox_table
text: cox_table() logistic_table() fit variable , fit one multivariable model, return single tidy table univariable multivariable estimates side side. Numeric variables contribute one row per-unit estimate; factors contribute one row per level reference level.

title: Regression tables for clinical variables — cox_table
code: cox_table(   data,   time,   event,   factors = NULL,   max_time = NULL,   multivariable = c("all", "significant", "none"),   significance = 0.05,   ci_level = 0.95 )  logistic_table(   data,   outcome,   factors = NULL,   positive = NULL,   multivariable = c("all", "significant", "none"),   significance = 0.05,   ci_level = 0.95 )

title: Regression tables for clinical variables — cox_table
text: data Data frame holding variables. time, event Column names follow-time event indicator used cox_table(). factors Character vector variable names analyse. Defaults every column data except time event columns. max_time Optional follow-limit cox_table(). Times beyond limit censored limit. multivariable variables enter multivariable model: "" (default), "significant", "none". significance Significance level used multivariable = "significant". ci_level Confidence level reported intervals. outcome Column name binary outcome used logistic_table(). positive Value outcome represents event.

title: Regression tables for clinical variables — cox_table
text: tibble one row per term columns term, variable, level, n, n_event, univariable estimate (hr_univariable or_univariable) interval p-value, corresponding multivariable columns.

title: Regression tables for clinical variables — cox_table
text: multivariable model includes requested variables default. multivariable = "significant" variables whose univariable likelihood-ratio test significance included, reproduces screening rule original helper functions.

title: Regression tables for clinical variables — cox_table
code: set.seed(42) dat <- data.frame(   time = rexp(60, 0.1),   event = rbinom(60, 1, 0.7),   age = rnorm(60, 60, 8),   stage = factor(sample(c("II", "III"), 60, replace = TRUE)) ) cox_table(dat, time = "time", event = "event") #> # A tibble: 2 × 13 #>   term   variable level     n n_event hr_univariable univ_ci_lower univ_ci_upper #>   <chr>  <chr>    <chr> <int>   <int>          <dbl>         <dbl>         <dbl> #> 1 age    age      NA       60      36          1.00          0.961          1.05 #> 2 stage… stage    III      60      36          0.968         0.495          1.89 #> # ℹ 5 more variables: univ_p <dbl>, hr_multivariable <dbl>, #> #   multi_ci_lower <dbl>, multi_ci_upper <dbl>, multi_p <dbl> set.seed(42) dat <- data.frame(   response = rbinom(60, 1, 0.4),   age = rnorm(60, 60, 8),   sex = factor(sample(c("F", "M"), 60, replace = TRUE)) ) logistic_table(dat, outcome = "response") #> # A tibble: 2 × 13 #>   term  variable level     n n_event or_univariable univ_ci_lower univ_ci_upper #>   <chr> <chr>    <chr> <int>   <int>          <dbl>         <dbl>         <dbl> #> 1 age   age      NA       60      31          1.03          0.961          1.11 #> 2 sexM  sex      M        60      31          0.729         0.256          2.08 #> # ℹ 5 more variables: univ_p <dbl>, or_multivariable <dbl>, #> #   multi_ci_lower <dbl>, multi_ci_upper <dbl>, multi_p <dbl>

what: Odds ratio for a marker with a binary outcome — odds_ratio
title: Odds ratio for a marker with a binary outcome — odds_ratio

title: Odds ratio for a marker with a binary outcome — odds_ratio
text: x Marker factor binarise. Continuous numeric values split optimal threshold; numeric, logical, character, factor inputs two distinct values used directly. outcome Binary outcome. Logical vectors coded TRUE event; numeric 0/1 vectors use 1 event. coding requires positive name event level. positive Value outcome represents event. cutoff Optional threshold supplied user. Values greater cutoff form high group. ci_level Confidence level AUC interval.

title: Odds ratio for a marker with a binary outcome — odds_ratio
text: tibble one row: threshold used, sample size, number events, group sizes, odds ratio Wald confidence interval, Wald p-value.

what: Resampling-based Cox screening of candidate markers — resample_cox
title: Resampling-based Cox screening of candidate markers — resample_cox
text: Repeatedly draws subsamples samples, fits univariable Cox model every candidate column, reports often candidate reached p_threshold. resampling screening previously provided calc_resamp_cox(), reported per-marker selection frequencies instead raw p-value matrix.

title: Resampling-based Cox screening of candidate markers — resample_cox
code: resample_cox(   expression,   time,   event,   ratio = 0.8,   times = 1000,   p_threshold = 0.05,   seed = NULL )

title: Resampling-based Cox screening of candidate markers — resample_cox
text: expression Numeric matrix data frame samples rows candidate markers columns. time, event Follow-time event indicator, one value per sample. ratio Fraction samples drawn resample. times Number resamples. p_threshold Significance threshold counts selection. seed Optional integer seed reproducible resampling.

title: Resampling-based Cox screening of candidate markers — resample_cox
text: tibble one row per candidate marker: number valid resamples, number resamples marker significant, selection fraction, median p-value.

title: Resampling-based Cox screening of candidate markers — resample_cox
text: function uses future framework. Set parallel plan calling use several workers, example future::plan(future::multisession).

title: Resampling-based Cox screening of candidate markers — resample_cox
code: set.seed(1) expr <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 5), nrow = 60, dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("g", 1:5))) time <- rexp(60) event <- rbinom(60, 1, 0.7) resample_cox(expr, time, event, times = 20, seed = 1) #> # A tibble: 5 × 5 #>   gene  n_valid n_significant fraction median_p #>   <chr>   <dbl>         <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1 g1         20             1     0.05    0.140 #> 2 g2         20             0     0       0.661 #> 3 g3         20             0     0       0.794 #> 4 g4         20             0     0       0.297 #> 5 g5         20             0     0       0.715

what: Summarise the diagnostic performance of a numeric marker — roc_summary
title: Summarise the diagnostic performance of a numeric marker — roc_summary
text: Computes area receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) confidence interval optimal operating point numeric marker binary outcome. tibble one row returned, result can combined across markers subgroups.

title: Summarise the diagnostic performance of a numeric marker — roc_summary
code: roc_summary(   marker,   outcome,   positive = NULL,   direction = "auto",   best_method = c("youden", "closest.topleft"),   ci_level = 0.95,   power = FALSE,   alternative = c("one.sided", "two.sided") )

title: Summarise the diagnostic performance of a numeric marker — roc_summary
text: marker Numeric vector marker values. outcome Binary outcome. Logical vectors coded TRUE event; numeric 0/1 vectors use 1 event. coding requires positive name event level. positive Value outcome represents event. direction Direction comparison passed pROC::roc(). "auto" lets pROC choose direction data; "<" ">" fix explicitly. best_method Method used choose optimal operating point, "youden" (default) "closest.topleft". ci_level Confidence level AUC interval. power TRUE, add power AUC test reported pROC::power.roc.test(). value may NA power estimated sample. alternative Alternative hypothesis used power estimate.

title: Summarise the diagnostic performance of a numeric marker — roc_summary
text: tibble one row: sample size, number events, AUC confidence interval, optimal threshold, sensitivity, specificity, positive negative predictive values, accuracy threshold.

title: Summarise the diagnostic performance of a numeric marker — roc_summary

what: Survival cut point optimising the Youden index — survival_cutoff
title: Survival cut point optimising the Youden index — survival_cutoff
text: Estimates Kaplan-Meier survival candidate cut point marker predict_time returns cut point maximises Youden index (sensitivity + specificity - 1), criterion long-unmaintained survivalROC package uses, computed directly survival::survfit(). Candidates drawn quantile grid keep computation bounded.

title: Survival cut point optimising the Youden index — survival_cutoff

title: Survival cut point optimising the Youden index — survival_cutoff

title: Survival cut point optimising the Youden index — survival_cutoff
text: tibble one row: optimal cutoff, Youden index (youden), time-dependent true positive rate (tp) false positive rate (fp) cut point, number observations.

title: clinstats 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Consolidates modernises statistical utilities curated colorectal cancer clinical datasets previously distributed separate gaofenglib curatedClinicalData repositories. roc_summary() replaces calc_logit(), tidy one-row output. odds_ratio() replaces calc_or(). cox_table() replaces factor_analysis_cox(). logistic_table() replaces factor_analysis_logit(). evaluate_model() replaces eval_logit(), train/test evaluation DeLong comparison two areas curve. survival_cutoff() replaces calc_cutoff_survivalroc() computes Kaplan-Meier Youden cut point directly survival::survfit() bounded quantile grid, long-unmaintained survivalROC package longer dependency. resample_cox() replaces calc_resamp_cox(), reports per-gene selection frequencies, defaults sequential future plan. clean_expression() replaces clean_dat(); gene identifier mapping now optional org.Hs.eg.db dependency. oncotype_crc() replaces calc_oncotypedx_crc(). tcga_clinical() replaces extract_tcga_clinical(). survival_response() replaces get_survival(). Removed environment-mutating helpers init_R() update_all(). exported functions return tibbles validate inputs clear error messages. cox_table() logistic_table() include every requested variable multivariable model default; multivariable = "significant" reproduces previous univariable-screening rule original helpers. Datasets clin_crc, clin_crc_gf, clin_crc_cell carried byte-identical curatedClinicalData, provenance documentation. Added Quarto analysis report template, testthat coverage, GitHub Actions checks, pkgdown site.
